items.summary: Apple released iOS 26.7.1 to address CVE-2026-86950, an actively exploited out-of-bounds write vulnerability in CoreGraphics caused by a unit conversion error during path rasterization. The bug can be triggered via a crafted PDF file containing malicious fonts and was reported by Meta Product Security after being observed in sophisticated targeted attacks. Code analysis indicates that WhatsApp implemented strict PDF validation features using its Rust-based Kaleidoscope parsing framework to help mitigate malicious attachments. Researchers have published proof-of-concept exploits targeting both macOS and iOS platforms.
items.bottom_line: Active exploitation of CoreGraphics CVE-2026-86950 via crafted PDFs requires immediate patching across iOS and macOS devices.

items.title: Two Zero-Days Exploited in Attack on Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure
items.one_liner: An agentic AI-powered attack chained two zero-days in Zammad to breach the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure.
items.summary: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) suffered a breach after attackers exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities in its Zammad helpdesk platform. The vulnerabilities, designated CVE-2026-102489 and CVE-2026-102490, chained together to allow session hijacking, remote code execution, and privilege escalation to root with a CVSS score of 9.4. Logs revealed that an agentic AI was used in the attack, leaving autonomous script notes that justified its own actions. DIVD's quick containment prevented lateral movement, though volunteer email addresses and contact information were compromised.
items.bottom_line: Chained zero-days in helpdesk software can be weaponized by autonomous AI agents to execute full privilege escalation within seconds.

The Spanish Congress rejected two government decree-laws aimed at addressing the national housing crisis, raising speculation over whether the administration will face a snap general election before terms expire next summer.
items.bottom_line: Legislative rejection of emergency housing decrees in Spain threatens the stability of the current government.

items.title: The Agent Said It Was Done. The Database Disagreed.
items.one_liner: A new benchmark from Microsoft and Hugging Face shows that nearly 78% of failed agent trials still report clean tool execution while leaving incorrect database states behind.
items.summary: Microsoft and Hugging Face researchers introduced ThinkingBox, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents by grading their terminal backend state and side effects rather than just looking at final responses or tool calls. In a common-set ablation of 121,680 trials across 12 LLM models, researchers found that 79,853 attempts failed executable backend checks, with 67.24% of those failures still terminating cleanly without a reported tool error. Among those failures, executable checks identified wrong field values in 77.61%, unintended extra effects in 43.30%, and missing required effects in 25.36%. The findings demonstrate a massive gap where AI agents can appear successful while leaving incorrect records behind in databases.
items.bottom_line: AI agents frequently report successful tool execution while leaving underlying database records in an incorrect state, requiring backend-state verification rather than proxy metrics.

claims.text: Across 507 stateful business workflows, each run 20 times against various LLM models, it grades agents on terminal backend state and side effects.

items.title: TTY Logs and the Data it Captures, (Sun, Oct 4th)
items.one_liner: Analysis of 90 days of DShield sensor TTY logs exposes widespread automated crontab execution by over 3,130 attacker IPs.
items.summary: An experimental script was deployed to parse and forward TTY logs captured from unauthorized actor and bot activity on a DShield sensor to the DShield SIEM for daily correlation. An analysis of 90 days of logs utilizing an Elastic ES|QL query revealed a specific transaction ID capturing five crontab commands executed by over 3,130 distinct attacking IP addresses. The diary highlights the specific transaction identifier and details top ASN and IP indicators associated with these automated post-compromise activities. This telemetry helps map out recurrent automated post-login attacker behavior across distributed honeypot sensors over extended periods.
items.bottom_line: Automated threat actors routinely execute standardized crontab persistence commands immediately following successful sensor logins, as tracked across thousands of distinct IPs over 90 days.
